chunks: Three [narrators] — Muhammad ibn Uthman said: Ahmad ibn Abi Khaythama narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Yazeed, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Ribaa'ah ibn Sayf, who said: We were with Shufiy al-Asbahi. He said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'After me there will be twelve caliphs.'

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّم: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number of leaders after him?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and others, explicitly predicts twelve successors (khalifa) following the Prophet, a narrative central to Shia theology for establishing the divine appointment of the Twelve Imams. While Sunni traditions also cite this prophecy, Shia scholars emphasize its specific application to the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing their leadership from the broader caliphate. The text serves as a critical scriptural basis for the concept of Imamah, linking prophetic foreknowledge directly to the lineage of Imams.
